newsitem.title: USA: U.S. detainee in North Korea is moved to a prison.
newsitem.headline: U.S. detainee in North Korea is moved to a prison.

text.p: An American being held in North Korea on spying charges has been transferred from a hotel to a jail, the State Department said on Wednesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the department had been informed of the move by Swedish diplomats who represent U.S. interests in North Korea and have made several visits to the detained man, Carl Hunziker, 26.

Hunziker, described by his family as a missionary, was arrested in North Korea on Aug. 24 after entering from China. U.S. officials have ridiculed North Korean allegations that he is a spy and have demanded his release.
Hunziker was held for some time in a hotel in a town about four hours' train ride from the capital, Pyongyang. Burns said he did not know where the prison was located.
The spokesman said Swedish diplomat Ake Lafquist was attempting to make a further visit to Hunziker to give him winter clothing.
Burns said U.S. officials had raised the Hunziker case again at a meeting on Tuesday with North Korean diplomats at the United Nations in New York, but he gave no details.
The State Department said on Tuesday it was encouraged by a recent North Korean statement describing Hunziker's case as a humanitarian one.
Burns said the move to a prison did not necessarily conflict with that assessment. "We've always felt that house arrest in a hotel was jail too," he told reporters.
